headline: One experiment
body: It's from 2004 and it takes about a minute to explain.
punch: Almost every height claim you've heard ignores it.

headline: The question
body: Why does bone growth slow down with age? Two possible answers. Something in your body is telling the plate to slow, or something in the plate itself is running down.
punch: Those predict different results. So test them.

headline: The setup
body: Take a growth plate from a young animal and put it in an old one. Take a plate from an old animal and put it in a young one. Then measure how fast each grows.

headline: If your body controlled it
body: A plate in a young recipient should grow fast regardless of where it came from, because the young body is sending stronger growth signals.
punch: That's the prediction from Tanner's model.

headline: What actually happened
body: Young plate in an old animal grew fast. Old plate in a young animal stayed slow. The growth rate tracked the age of the plate, not the age of the body it was in.
punch: Every time. Not a marginal effect.

headline: Which means
body: Not hormones. Not the brain. Not systemic signals. The plate carries its own history and that history determines how much growing it has left.
punch: Your bones keep their own score.

headline: And that reframes
body: If the limit is inside the plate, then anything acting systemically is working on the wrong level. That's why cartilage targeted delivery exists as a research idea at all.

headline: What it doesn't tell you
body: It shows the capacity is intrinsic and finite. It doesn't show what the capacity is made of, or how fusion executes. Those are still open.
punch: One clean answer. Several open questions.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
